details:
Project Details – Junior Astronaut Mission Trainer

Junior Astronaut Mission Trainer is an interactive educational game designed to introduce children aged 7–12 to space exploration, astronomy, and astronaut training in a fun and engaging way.

The project allows children to experience different space-related missions through interactive challenges, educational activities, quizzes, and problem-solving tasks. Players can learn about astronauts, planets, space environments, and the challenges of exploring space while developing their curiosity, critical thinking, and decision-making skills.

Our main goal is to make space science more accessible and enjoyable for young learners. By combining education with gaming, we aim to encourage children to explore science, technology, engineering, and mathematics (STEM) and inspire the next generation of scientists, engineers, and astronauts.

We developed this project using HTML, CSS, and JavaScript. HTML provides the structure, CSS creates the visual design and user interface, and JavaScript makes the game interactive and functional. We focused on creating a colorful, space-themed environment with simple navigation and child-friendly activities.

The creative aspect of our project is its astronaut training concept. Instead of learning only through traditional lessons, children can explore space-related topics by completing missions and challenges. We wanted to make learning feel like a real space adventure.

During development, our team considered the target age group, ease of use, educational value, accessibility, visual design, and the importance of making scientific information understandable for children.

Our team, PARDIFEN, believes that learning about space should be exciting and available to everyone. Through Junior Astronaut Mission Trainer, we hope to inspire children to ask questions, discover new things, and dream beyond Earth.
